name: skriker

attributes.attribute: British figure that warns of coming death
shifts shape into a large black dog
similar warning figure of the Gaelic world

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The skriker is a figure of the British folk tradition. Its name comes from a word that means a trash or a scrap. The skriker tells that a death is close. It appears, like the banshee, to warn of the loss to come. It walks the forests of Yorkshire and of Lancashire, where it cries through the night. Like the fairy folk it can shift its shape. The skriker may turn itself into a huge black dog, and that shape is hard to face. The one who sees it knows that death will follow. The dog form is only one of its shapes. The skriker keeps to the northern lanes and carries the cold sign of the death of a life with it, moving from hedge to hedge until the news reaches the house that will mourn.
